fuel_consumption.source_quote: Based on projected 2010 fuel usage, such an increase would result in an increase to Aircraft fuel expense of approximately $499 million in 2010, inclusive of the impact of effective fuel hedge instruments outstanding at December 31, 2009

instrument_type_details.notes: Primarily heating oil option and collar contracts as cash flow hedges. As of Dec 31, 2009: 20 million barrels of jet fuel covered by outstanding derivative contracts to be settled over next 24 months. Net losses in fuel expense 2009: ~($651)M; 2008: ~$380M gains; 2007: ~$239M gains. Fair value at Dec 31, 2009: $57M (asset, recovered from ($450)M liability at Dec 31, 2008). Net ~$74M in losses to be reclassified from AOCI to earnings in next 12 months as of Dec 31, 2009 (including losses from 2008 bankrupt counterparty).

warnings: Fuel consumption in gallons not explicitly stated in this filing; only dollar-based sensitivity disclosures provided. Note 7 states 20 million barrels outstanding at Dec 31, 2009 across next 24 months.
Pct hedged as of 'January 2010' (early 2010), not as of Dec 31, 2009.
Volume outstanding from Note 7 is in BARRELS (20 million barrels), not gallons — this is a BARREL-denominated position disclosure.
Jan 2010: Venezuela currency devaluation from 2.15 to 4.30 bolivars/USD caused $53M loss recognized in Jan 2010.
